affected_parts.evidence: The most common symptom of leaf scald is a white line about 1–2 mm wide (also called a pencil line) on the leaf... Ultimately, the entire plant dies.

summary.value: A white 1-2 mm 'pencil line' on the leaf running parallel to the veins from midrib to margin with a diffuse yellow border, progressing to brown necrosis from the leaf tip or margin with inward-curling, scalded-looking leaves and eventual plant death.
summary.evidence: The most common symptom of leaf scald is a white line about 1–2 mm wide (also called a pencil line) on the leaf. This line extends from the midrib to the leaf margin running parallel to the veins. A diffuse yellow border of varying widths runs parallel to the pencil line. The pencil line may have areas of reddish discoloration along part of its length. As the disease progresses, brown, dead tissue (necrosis) develops from the leaf tip or leaf margin and eventually extends the entire leaf. Leaves look burned and curl inward, giving them a scalded appearance–hence the disease's name. Ultimately, the entire plant dies.

diagnostic_features.value: A narrow white 'pencil line' (1-2 mm wide) extending from midrib to leaf margin parallel to veins, bordered by a diffuse yellow margin, sometimes with reddish discoloration, leading to burned-looking, inward-curling scalded leaves.

disease_name.evidence: SSAGR203/SC003: Sugarcane Eyespot Disease

pathogen_scientific_name.evidence: Eyespot disease is caused by the fungus Bipolaris sacchari .

type_of_disease.evidence: Eyespot disease is caused by the fungus Bipolaris sacchari .

affected_parts.evidence: The first observable symptoms are minute water-soaked spots that usually occur on young leaves

summary.value: Minute water-soaked spots appear first on young leaves, developing into reddish-brown elliptical lesions with yellowish-brown margins, often accompanied by long reddish-brown to yellowish-brown streaks (runners) extending toward the leaf tip in cooler conditions.
summary.evidence: The first observable symptoms are minute water-soaked spots that usually occur on young leaves (Comstock and Steiner 1989). Typical mature eyespot symptoms are characterized by a reddish-brown elliptical lesion (0.5–4.0 mm long, 0.5–2.0 mm wide) with yellowish-brown margins (Figure 1). Reddish-brown to yellowish-brown streaks, sometimes called "runners," extend upward from individual lesions toward the leaf tip.

diagnostic_features.value: Reddish-brown elliptical lesion (0.5–4.0 mm long, 0.5–2.0 mm wide) with yellowish-brown margins, with reddish-brown to yellowish-brown 'runners' (streaks 3–6 mm wide and 30–90 cm long) extending upward from lesions toward the leaf tip in cooler temperatures.
diagnostic_features.evidence: Typical mature eyespot symptoms are characterized by a reddish-brown elliptical lesion (0.5–4.0 mm long, 0.5–2.0 mm wide) with yellowish-brown margins (Figure 1). Reddish-brown to yellowish-brown streaks, sometimes called "runners," extend upward from individual lesions toward the leaf tip. These streaks are 3–6 mm wide and 30–90 cm long.
